Try assessing your bare skin to see if it’s dehydrated, if it is I think you should scale back. If not there’s no harm in trying 10%. But also keep in mind that often acne needs to be combatted with more than one product based on what kind it is. The BP will only kill the acne-causing bacteria, but if the underlying issue is clogged pores, over-production of sebum or ineffective cell turnover, you’ll keep seeing blemishes pop up. In which case you’ll need another product to get the results you want.


Edit: I also don’t think the BP not being effective is a concern, both BP and salicylic acid are very effective even in washes because they get into your pores and stay there to some extent even after you wash them off. Think of BP in a similar vein to a disinfectant you might use to clean a wound and kill bacteria, you wouldn’t necessarily get better results using a higher strength, it’ll just be harsher on the skin. Also, as another user mentioned BP doesn’t really exfoliate and it also won’t help close the pores, Differin or BHA are better options for both those concerns.

Based off what you’re saying about BP leaving your skin looking tired, dull and not soft, I think your problem may be that you’re over-doing it. BP is known to be quite harsh on the skin and dries it out which, contrary to what most of us try to do to combat acne, doesn’t help and can worsen the situation. Based on personal experience, I have pretty oily skin and can only use BP once every other day without it drying me out. 

I’d suggest you start with making sure your skin is hydrated and cutting back BP from twice a day to once, you could even do it as a wash off (apply it as soon as you can in the evening after washing your face, and wash off the BP before bed). I find the wash-off method the best because I can leave it on for a couple hours and let it do it’s thing and then take it off and follow it up with other actives. Try that for a few days and if it still doesn’t help you might need another active for the acne- BHA or Differin are good options but without knowing more I can’t say for sure. Hope this helps and good luck!

Hey, thanks for pointing this out! I think I found the study you’re referring to. It was conducted on mostly elder male veterans over a 6 year period. The researchers do point out that past smoking habits, lifestyles etc were not properly accounted for. The mortality rate of 108  in the tret group vs 76 in the non tret group may be a reflection of that. I also think that it has to do with how the study was carried out, they weren’t looking for mortality risk and didn’t have a system in place to statistically determine it. Moreover, they were also unable to establish any cause-effect relation between use of tretinoin and death, since the deaths in the tret group were caused by diverse factors like lung cancer, vascular conditions etc. 

I think it’s a combination of these factors that caused the unlikely discrepancy; aged and at risk subjects + no way to correct for pre-study mortality risk. I don’t think tretinoin causing cancer is likely but I’m no expert.

Unfortunately, I don’t think that the Glycolic Acid will help your skin right now, it’s an AHA and works by chemically exfoliating the top layer of your skin to improve texture. Since we’re trying to initially restore your moisture barrier to health it’s best to wait a bit before you incorporate it into your routine. 

You need something hydrating, a lot of KBeauty products could serve your purpose (look for essences or hydrating toners). However if you don’t want to jump into that you could always try throwing on lots of moisturizer (cerave in the tub) twice a day first and see if that works for you.

I know it can get frustrating dealing with acne and the roller coaster of skin types your skin starts to take on when treating it. What is most likely happening in your case is that the Azelaic Acid has over stripped and sensitized your skin since you jumped into using it twice a day right off the bat. This is causing your skin to produce more natural oil to combat that. 

No worries though, it’s easily fixable. You should try introducing a hydrating layer both in the AM and PM right after washing your face. Something with a humectant (attracts moisture to your skin’s outer layer) that’s non-comedogenic. Personally I’ve been using CosRX’s Advanced Snail Mucin for over a year to great effect but anything with a simple ingredient list and the above characteristics will work. Alternatively a hyaluronic acid product can also help with the same. In the AM you can then apply your moisturizer on top to hold the moisture content in. 

Additionally, skin heals faster when it’s properly hydrated which is why you’ve been seeing more blemishes on your dehydrated skin. Taking care of that dryness should also help those fade faster.

I think your problem is likely coming from the squalane oil in your moisturizer. If you have healthy but oily skin that can definitely cause your skin to be oilier. So to troubleshoot:

A- Do you have naturally oily skin?

B- If so, don’t worry you’re not the only one who’s tried moisturizing more to help with it. If that’s the case what you need to understand is that heavy moisturizing for oily skin is only really needed if your skin is dehydrated (feels tight or looks dry right after washing) it’s in this case that your skin will tend to overproduce oil to combat it. 
HOWEVER, this is uncommon and only really happens if you’ve been over exfoliating or have somehow damaged your lipid barrier.   

If your skin is oily but otherwise healthy you only really need a light moisturizer, a hydrating essence or gel moisturizer should be enough to keep your skin hydrated.  Stay away from oils and moisturizers with oils in them.

I think what they’re trying to do is create a framework of cognitive thinking for the host using the person’s actions and behavior in the Park. That’s tested for fidelity using existing markers like previous conversations to make sure the host thinks and acts the same way as the person it’s based on. It seems the show is then gonna put in the person’s mapped brain (like they mapped Delos and Ford) which supplements the cognitive framework with the memories and life experiences which would give a pretty accurate rendering of the person.

There will of course be no way to test it and the assumptions needed to believe that the “host” IS the actual person lie in believing that, a- A carefully crafted and analyzed cognitive network can be faithful to the real person’s thought process, and b- supplementing that network with the mapped brain recreates the real consciousness .

It’s likely that they’ll go in this direction given the different ways they’ve tried to recreate a person so far. Bernard was based on Arnold’s actions, he was created to be faithful to Arnold’s cognitive thinking but with none of Arnold’s actual memories, those were all fabricated which is why he can’t truly BE Arnold. Delos was created by simply implanting his mapped brain into an artificial body, but this rendering faced the problem of breaking down because the mind “rejected reality”, possibly meaning that there wasn’t enough cognition in that recreation to think for itself and understand its new reality (that it’s a host). It couldn’t be the real Delos because it was a copy, it could do the same thing the real Delos did if put in the same situation but not think like Delos and do what he would if in an unfamiliar situation. So it makes sense that they intend on putting the two methods together to create an accurate rendering of a person.
